contexts.text: Ye have made our odour to stink... () = that they have so great an aversion to our compliance... To make to stink = aversion.
As a stink is a thing which is held in aversion, it is used in the Word for aversion. Illustrated... Here stink = abominable evil.
The reason their odour ia said to stink in their eyes, is that all in evils and falsities are averse to goods; and truths stink to them.

That those in evils and the derivative falsities have a stink, is very evident from the Hells called cadaverous, where there are assassins and those very tenacious of revenge; and from the Hells called excrementitious, where there are adulterers and those who have had filthy pleasures as their end. When these Hells are opened, intolerable stinks exhale from them; but these stinks are not smelled except by those who have the interiors, which are of the spirit, open. But still those in these Hells apperceive these stinks as grateful, and therefore they love to live in these stinks. For they are like those animals which live in carcasses and excrements, and there have the delight of their life. When those Spirits come outside the sphere of those stinks, sweet and grateful odours are noisome and in the highest degree ungrateful to them.
See Stink. DP 340:6.
The river shall stink () = aversion for the memory-knowledge of truth. To stink = aversion.

In the other life, nothing is more abominable, and consequently nothing stinks more disagreeably, than profaned truth... It is circumstanced as is the stink of a carcase, which is produced when living flesh is dying; for falsity does not smell unless it is united to truth, nor evil unless it is united to good: each is smelled, not from itself, but from its opposite, in its true character; from which it may be evident how greatly profaned truth must stink; for profaned truth is falsity conjoined with truth...
One of which (beautiful women) is wholly rotten and stinking from scortation.
The land stank () = what is consequently noisome and repulsive.

Their damnation is smelled by the stink and fetor which exhales from them more than from those with whom such (knowledges) have not been a matter of faith... In general, if an evil Spirit approaches a heavenly Society, where there is charity, a stink is plainly smelled from him. So in particular, where, in the same subject, there have been such things as are of Heaven... and also such things as are of Hell.
See Stink. CL 431:end.
Whereas falsities from evil may be compared to unclean foods, which are inwardly putrid.
A corrupt tree makes evil fruits ().
In Heaven, this heresy (that God has infused Himself into men) stinks like a carcase.
See Stench here. AE 1057:7.
They might have known that... consequently evil in itself is stinking...
Truth falsified (there) stinks in the nostrils of the Angels.
From the body (of that devil) there was exhaled a stinking and unclean heat.
Truth falsified in itself is putrefying falsity; for in Heaven it stinks.
Fruits which from their spring are rotten within.
The damnation of those who would perish through evils, is signified by the stink of their carcasses shall come up ()... Stink = their damnation.
Hence it is that from the brothels in the Hells there pour forth stinks which excite vomiting.
As the place where he had stood stank from (his murdering of truths) I hurried away home. For in the Spiritual World Divine truth falsified by satans stinks like the filth of the streets.
